Staszow Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Staszów, Poland

Demolished. Jews first appeared in Staszów records in 1578, but a 1610 blood-libel accusation drove the emerging community out until resettlement began in the late 17th century. A 1718 privilege from town owner Elżbieta Szaniawska (confirmed 1772) permitted Jewish settlement, trade, and religious institutions; population reached 64.2% (3,947) by 1865, with Staszów becoming a major Hasidic center hosting two interwar yeshivas. During WWII, 8,000-9,000 Jews were held in the town's ghetto, mostly deported to Bełżec in November 1942 with some shot on-site, and the rest sent to Treblinka through 1943. This original cemetery, established following the 1718 privilege, was in use for less than a century before closing in 1819 for sanitary reasons; postwar development built a kindergarten playground on the site.
